summary: Max Scheler (1874–1928) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at Jena (~1899–1907), Munich (~1907–1910), Göttingen, and Cologne (~1919–1928), and taught Edward Conze.

Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD). He taught at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936), founding the Heidelberg Institute for Buddhology in 1928.
May Oung (1880–1926) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1904 to 1907 and founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Cambridge, and Yale (PhD ~2002). She held a post at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a professor of history at Harvard University around 2009.
Mayum Chonying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a General Council member there from 1964 to 1965.

Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She held a lecturer post at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and was attested as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University in 2026.

McKim Marriott (1924–2024) worked in Indology and anthropology. He studied at Harvard under Clyde Kluckhohn and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1948–1955), where he served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences from ~1957 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University (PhD). He has taught at the University of Colombo (~2002), Buddhist and Pali University, and PGIPBS.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Meei-Hwa Chern works in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under John C. Raines and served as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.
Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

Megumu Honda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells, and later served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

Mei Ching Hsuan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger, also studying under Dieter Schuh, and served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962) and served there as a professor (attested 1963 and 2007).

Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch, and at Paris. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at the University of Michigan and earned his PhD at the University of Washington (~1968), later serving as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Merab Mamardashvili (1930–1990) was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980), and also studied under Kathryn A. Cissell.
